Header.title: I traded the microscope for code.
Header.intro: I’m {name}. I studied biotechnology engineering and worked in a neurobiology lab before moving into software. Today I build the quote, payment and after-sales flows for Seguros Falabella with React, Next.js, NestJS and Strapi, and AI is part of my everyday work.
Header.channels: Cultured neuron, three channels. Switch one off to see each layer.

About.title: From the lab to web development.
About.lab: I studied biotechnology engineering and spent three years in a neurobiology lab doing statistics, data analysis and bioinformatics. That’s where I learned not to trust a result until I can reproduce it.
About.code: In 2016 I started building online stores, and since 2022 I’ve worked as a full-stack developer. The lab habit came with me: I test, measure and review before I call anything done.

Projects.title: Five stages, <hl>one customer</hl>.
Projects.body: Five applications that, in order, cover what a person does with their insurance: get a quote, buy it, pay for it, sign in to their account and handle requests.

Architecture.title: Under the hood, <hl>one architecture</hl>.
Architecture.body: The five applications share the same layers: a front end in Next.js or React, NestJS services with hexagonal architecture, content in Strapi and data in MongoDB. Each layer has a single job, so a front end can be migrated or an integration swapped without touching the business rules.
Architecture.rule: Dependencies point inward: the domain knows nothing about NestJS, MongoDB or HTTP.
Architecture.skill: It’s the same pattern I taught the agent in a skill

Ai.title: I use AI every day. And I <hl>review everything</hl> it writes.
Ai.body: I come from analyzing data in a lab, so I treat a language model like any other instrument: fast and useful, but I don’t trust it until I’ve checked.

Skills.title: What I work with.
Skills.body: Each well is a technology I use, sorted by channel: frontend, backend, AI, data and tools.
